claims.text: At high temperatures, FeNiCrCoCu thin-film wear resistance is primarily governed by formation of a stable protective oxide layer at grain boundaries.
A grain-boundary oxide layer inhibits thermal softening of the coating.
A grain-boundary oxide layer suppresses grain-boundary sliding under mechanical load.
The as-deposited baseline coating has a polycrystalline microstructure with relatively clean grain boundaries.
Controlled pre-oxidation in air can promote a thin, adherent oxide along the coating grain boundaries.
The proposed comparison is between a pre-oxidized coating and an otherwise comparable as-deposited coating.
The target wear-test temperature is approximately 600°C.
A pre-formed grain-boundary oxide acts as a thermal and mechanical barrier.
The oxide barrier limits diffusion-driven softening.
The oxide barrier limits grain-boundary sliding.
Limiting diffusion-driven softening and grain-boundary sliding enhances high-temperature wear resistance.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have lower wear rates than as-deposited coatings under identical high-temperature sliding conditions.
Pre-oxidized coatings will show less material removal than as-deposited coatings.
Pre-oxidized coatings will resist deformation better than as-deposited coatings.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to FeNiCrCoCu protective thin films on conventional-metal substrates near 600°C under sliding load.
Behavior outside the stated temperature and loading regime may differ.
Oxide-formation kinetics and long-term oxide stability during prolonged high-temperature exposure are not fully understood.
The optimum pre-oxidation conditions for obtaining a uniform protective layer remain undetermined.
